question: to the Commission Marie-Luce Brasier-Clain (PfE), Mathilde Androuët (PfE), Volker Schnurrbusch (ESN), Valérie Deloge (PfE), Catherine Griset (PfE), António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Alvise Pérez (NI), Jorge Martín Frías (PfE), Julie Rechagneux (PfE), Margarita de la Pisa Carrión (PfE), Pierre Pimpie (PfE) Subject:

The Commission has launched a revision of the guidelines on State aid in the air transport sector to take account of decarbonisation goals in particular. The outermost regions (ORs), recognised under Article 349 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, continue to grapple with permanent structural constraints as a result of their remoteness, insularity and reliance on air transport. Air transport is essential to ensuring they remain connected to the mainland and have access to care, education, employment and local economic development. In view of the above: 1.

How does the Commission intend to ensure that the revision of the guidelines and decarbonisation objectives does not result in fewer air connections or higher travel costs for residents in the outermost regions?

Does it intend to maintain or adapt support mechanisms for strategic air links serving the ORs, including links with nearby third countries, as those links help open up those territories, keep them connected to the mainland and contribute to their economic development?

How does the Commission intend to take into account the complementary nature of certain airport infrastructure located in the ORs when that infrastructure specific access and resilience needs in those regions?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.9.2026) The draft Air Transport guidelines1, as recently published for public consultation from 11 May 2026 – 11 June 2026, specifically address the constraints faced by remote regions, including outermost regions. For example, they provide for a bonus for investment aid projects and when it comes to the designation of outermost regions airports as Services of General Economic Interest. In the parallel, as part of the revision of the General Block Exemption Regulation2 the Commission proposes to raise the notification threshold for operating and investment aid to airports from 200,000 to 500,000 passengers per year, which will considerably simplify the granting of aid to many airports, including in the outermost regions. The Commission is currently assessing the feedback to the public consultation. This will feed into the revision, and the Commission will ensure that both the special situation of outermost regions and all relevant EU objectives such as territorial and social cohesion, regional development and decarbonisation are duly considered. When it comes to safeguarding essential air services at affordable terms, the existing State aid framework allows Member States to impose public service obligations pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1008/2008 (intra-EU routes) or rely on social aid (in principle also for routes connecting an EU airport to a non-EU airport). These possibilities remain unaffected by the ongoing revision.
